subproblems.title: Every n-dimensional subspace is a rotated horizontal plane
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers n and l and every linear subspace T of R^{n+l} = Amb n l with dim T = n, there is a linear isometry equivalence q of R^{n+l} such that rotatedPlane q = q(horizontalPlane n l) = T, where horizontalPlane n l is the span of the first n standard basis vectors e_{castAdd l i}, i < n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), Module.finrank ℝ T = n → ∃ q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ, rotatedPlane q = T
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Notation. Let E := Amb n l = EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n+l)); finrank E = n + l (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). For k in Fin (n+l) let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1, the standard orthonormal basis. By definition horizontalPlane n l = span{e_{Fin.castAdd l i} : i in Fin n} and rotatedPlane q = map q (horizontalPlane n l).
2. Orthonormal basis of T. Since finrank T = n, the orthonormal basis stdOrthonormalBasis R T, reindexed along finrank T = n, is an orthonormal basis (u_i)_{i in Fin n} of T. Viewed in E (the inclusion T -> E is a linear isometry), (u_i) is an orthonormal family in E, and span_R{u_i : i in Fin n} = T, because the span in E of the image of a basis of T is the image of T under the inclusion, i.e. T itself.
3. Extension. Define v : Fin (n+l) -> E by v := Fin.append u 0, so v(Fin.castAdd l i) = u_i, and let s := range (Fin.castAdd l). The restriction of v to s is orthonormal: it is the orthonormal family u composed with the bijection Fin n -> s, i |-> Fin.castAdd l i. Since finrank E = n + l = card (Fin (n+l)), Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq gives an orthonormal basis b : OrthonormalBasis (Fin (n+l)) R E with b(Fin.castAdd l i) = u_i for every i in Fin n.
4. The isometry. Let q := b.repr.symm. Because E = EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n+l)), q is a linear isometry equivalence of E = Amb n l onto itself, and q(e_k) = b k for every k (OrthonormalBasis.repr_symm_single).
5. Conclusion. rotatedPlane q = map q (span{e_{castAdd l i} : i}) = span{q(e_{castAdd l i}) : i} (Submodule.map_span) = span{b(castAdd l i) : i} = span{u_i : i} = T, by steps 2 to 4.
proof_key_steps: Take an orthonormal basis (u_i)_{i<n} of T (finrank T = n)
Place it at the indices castAdd l i and extend it to an orthonormal basis b of R^{n+l} (Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension_of_card_eq)
Let q := b.repr.symm, so q(e_k) = b_k
rotatedPlane q = span{q e_{castAdd l i}} = span{u_i} = T

subproblems.title: Dimension and distance estimates for a rotated linear graph plane
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, q a linear isometry equivalence of R^{n+l}, A : R^n -> R^l a continuous linear map with Hilbert-Schmidt norm |A| := hsNorm A, and S := span{q(graphPoint(v, A v)) : v in R^n}. Then (i) dim S = n; (ii) dist(x, S) <= dist(x, rotatedPlane q) + |A| ||x|| for every x in R^{n+l}; (iii) dist(q(graphPoint(x', y)) - q(graphPoint(0, c)), S) <= ||y - (c + A x')|| for all x' in R^n and y, c in R^l; (iv) ||x'|| <= ||q(graphPoint(x', y)) - q(graphPoint(0, c))|| for the same x', y, c; (v) ||q(graphPoint(0, c))|| = ||c|| for every c in R^l. Here dist(z, P) = infDist z P.

subproblems.natural_proof:
0. Facts about graphPoint, from the definition graphPoint x y = toLp 2 (Fin.append (ofLp x) (ofLp y)) in R^{n+l} = EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n+l)).
(G1) Linearity: graphPoint (x + x') (y + y') = graphPoint x y + graphPoint x' y' and graphPoint (a x) (a y) = a graphPoint x y; hence graphPoint x y - graphPoint x' y' = graphPoint (x - x') (y - y'). These are coordinatewise identities for Fin.append.
(G2) Norm: ||graphPoint x y||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||y||^2, because the squared Euclidean norm is the sum of the squared coordinates and Fin.sum_univ_add splits the sum over Fin (n+l) into the first n and the last l coordinates. Hence ||x|| <= ||graphPoint x y|| and ||graphPoint 0 y|| = ||y||.
(G3) Every z in R^{n+l} equals graphPoint a b with a := (z(Fin.castAdd l i))_{i in Fin n} and b := (z(Fin.natAdd n j))_{j in Fin l} (Fin.append_castAdd_natAdd).
(G4) horizontalPlane n l = {graphPoint v 0 : v in R^n}: the generator e_{castAdd l i} equals graphPoint (single i 1) 0, so by (G1) the span of the generators is the range of the linear map v |-> graphPoint v 0.
(G5) Operator bound: ||A a|| <= |A| ||a|| for a in R^n. Indeed a = sum_i a_i e_i, so ||A a|| <= sum_i |a_i| ||A e_i|| <= (sum_i a_i^2)^{1/2} (sum_i ||A e_i||^2)^{1/2} = ||a|| |A| by Cauchy-Schwarz, since hsNormSq A = sum_i ||A e_i||^2 and |A| = sqrt(hsNormSq A).
1. (i) Let Phi : R^n -> R^{n+l}, Phi(v) := q(graphPoint v (A v)). By (G1) and the linearity of A and q, Phi is linear, so S = span(range Phi) = range Phi (the range of a linear map is a subspace). Phi is injective because ||Phi v|| = ||graphPoint v (A v)|| >= ||v|| by (G2) (q is an isometry). Hence dim S = dim R^n = n (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj).
2. (v) ||q(graphPoint 0 c)|| = ||graphPoint 0 c|| = ||c|| by (G2).
3. (iv) By (G1), q(graphPoint x' y) - q(graphPoint 0 c) = q(graphPoint x' (y - c)), whose norm is ||graphPoint x' (y - c)|| >= ||x'|| by (G2).
4. (iii) Let z := q(graphPoint x' y) - q(graphPoint 0 c). Phi(x') lies in S and, by (G1), z - Phi(x') = q(graphPoint (x' - x') (y - c - A x')) = q(graphPoint 0 (y - (c + A x'))). Hence dist(z, S) <= ||z - Phi(x')|| = ||y - (c + A x')|| by (G2).
5. (ii) Let x in R^{n+l} and write q^{-1} x = graphPoint a b by (G3).

Combining (a) and (b): dist(x, S) <= dist(x, rotatedPlane q) + |A| ||x||.

subproblems.title: Hausdorff integrals over a rotated Lipschitz graph
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, q a linear isometry equivalence of R^{n+l}, D a measurable subset of R^n, L >= 0, and f : R^n -> R^l L-Lipschitz on D. Put F(x') := q(graphPoint(x', f(x'))), so that q '' graphOver f D = F(D). Then for every measurable g : R^{n+l} -> [0, infinity], the integral of g over q '' graphOver f D with respect to H^n = μHE[n] is at most (1 + L^2)^{n/2} = sqrt(1 + L^2)^n times the Lebesgue integral of g(F(x')) over x' in D.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (D : Set (Rn n)) (L : ℝ≥0), MeasurableSet D → LipschitzOnWith L f D → ∀ g : Amb n ℓ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g → ∫⁻ x in q '' graphOver f D, g x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (1 + (L : ℝ) ^ 2) ^ n) * ∫⁻ x' in D, g (q (graphPoint x' (f x')))
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Graph facts. From graphPoint x y = toLp 2 (Fin.append (ofLp x) (ofLp y)): graphPoint x y - graphPoint x' y' = graphPoint (x - x') (y - y') (coordinatewise), and ||graphPoint x y||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||y||^2 (split the coordinate sum over Fin (n+l) with Fin.sum_univ_add).
2. F is Lipschitz on D. For x', y' in D, since q is a linear isometry, ||F x' - F y'||^2 = ||graphPoint (x' - y') (f x' - f y')||^2 = ||x' - y'||^2 + ||f x' - f y'||^2 <= (1 + L^2) ||x' - y'||^2. So F is K-Lipschitz on D with K := sqrt(1 + L^2), regarded as an element of R>=0; in particular F is continuous on D.
3. Image bound. For every set E contained in D: μHE[n](F(E)) <= K^n vol(E). Indeed μHE[n] = c_n • μH[n] on every Borel metric space, with the same scalar c_n := addHaarScalarFactor (volume on EuclideanSpace R (Fin n)) μH[n] (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def). As F is K-Lipschitz on E, μH[n](F(E)) <= K^n μH[n](E) (LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le with d = n >= 0); multiplying by c_n gives μHE[n](F(E)) <= K^n μHE[n](E), and on R^n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) one has μHE[n] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
4. Push-forward. Let μ_D := volume.restrict D. Since D is measurable and F is continuous on D, F is AEMeasurable for μ_D (ContinuousOn.aemeasurable). Let ν := Measure.map F μ_D. For every measurable B in R^{n+l}, ν(B) = μ_D(F^{-1}(B)) (map_apply_of_aemeasurable) = vol(F^{-1}(B) ∩ D) (Measure.restrict_apply', valid for an arbitrary set because D is measurable).
5. Comparison of measures. Put Γ := q '' graphOver f D; Γ = F(D) (Set.image_image). For measurable B, B ∩ Γ = F(D ∩ F^{-1}(B)) (a point F(x') with x' in D lies in B iff x' lies in F^{-1}(B)). By step 3 applied to E := D ∩ F^{-1}(B), (μHE[n].restrict Γ)(B) = μHE[n](B ∩ Γ) <= K^n vol(D ∩ F^{-1}(B)) = K^n ν(B). Hence μHE[n].restrict Γ <= K^n • ν as measures (Measure.le_iff: it suffices to compare measurable sets).
6. Integrals. For measurable g >= 0, ∫⁻_Γ g dμHE[n] = ∫⁻ g d(μHE[n].restrict Γ) <= ∫⁻ g d(K^n • ν) (lintegral_mono' with the inequality of measures) = K^n ∫⁻ g dν (lintegral_smul_measure) = K^n ∫⁻_D g(F x') dx' (lintegral_map', g measurable and F AEMeasurable for μ_D). Finally K^n = ENNReal.ofReal(sqrt(1 + L^2)^n), the constant in the claim.
proof_key_steps: F(x') = q(graphPoint x' (f x')) is sqrt(1 + L^2)-Lipschitz on D
Lipschitz image bound for μH[n], rescaled to μHE[n], with μHE[n] = volume on R^n: μHE[n](F(E)) <= K^n vol(E) for E ⊆ D
μHE[n] restricted to F(D) is <= K^n times the push-forward of vol restricted to D under F (compare on measurable sets)
Integrate g and change variables with lintegral_map'

subproblems.title: One-dimensional sup bound by the L^2 norms of a Lipschitz function and of its derivative
subproblems.statement: Let l be a natural number, a > 0, K >= 0, and w : R^1 -> R^l (R^1 = EuclideanSpace R (Fin 1)) K-Lipschitz on the closed ball B̄_a(0). Then for every x in B̄_a(0): ||w(x)|| <= ((2a)^{-1} ∫_{B_a(0)} ||w||^2)^{1/2} + (2a ∫_{B_a(0)} hsNormSq(Dw))^{1/2}, where B_a(0) is the open ball, Dw(y) := fderiv w y, and the integrals are Bochner integrals for Lebesgue measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (ℓ : ℕ) (w : Rn 1 → Rn ℓ) (a : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0), 0 < a → LipschitzOnWith K w (closedBall 0 a) → ∀ x ∈ closedBall (0 : Rn 1) a, ‖w x‖ ≤ Real.sqrt ((2 * a)⁻¹ * ∫ y in ball (0 : Rn 1) a, ‖w y‖ ^ 2) + Real.sqrt (2 * a * ∫ y in ball (0 : Rn 1) a, hsNormSq (fderiv ℝ w y))
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. Interval coordinates. Let e := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 in R^1 and ι : R -> R^1, ι(t) := t e. ι is a linear isometry equivalence (||ι t|| = |t|, inverse z |-> z 0) mapping [-a, a] onto B̄_a(0) and (-a, a) onto B_a(0), and it is measure preserving from Lebesgue measure on R to volume on R^1 (the inverse of the composition of EuclideanSpace.measurableEquiv and MeasurableEquiv.funUnique, both volume preserving). Hence for every function φ on R^1, ∫_{B_a(0)} φ = ∫_{(-a,a)} φ(ι t) dt.
2. Let W := w ∘ ι : R -> R^l. W is K-Lipschitz on [-a, a], hence continuous there.
3. Derivatives. For every t, hsNormSq(fderiv w (ι t)) = ||deriv W t||^2. Indeed hsNormSq B = ||B e||^2 for B : R^1 ->L R^l (the defining sum has the single index 0). If w is differentiable at ι t, the chain rule gives deriv W t = fderiv w (ι t) (ι 1) = fderiv w (ι t) e. If w is not differentiable at ι t, then W is not differentiable at t (otherwise w = W ∘ ι^{-1} would be differentiable at ι t), so fderiv w (ι t) = 0 and deriv W t = 0.
4. Integrability. By Rademacher's theorem (LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem for W on [-a, a]; at interior points differentiability within [-a, a] is differentiability), W is differentiable at almost every t in (-a, a), and there ||deriv W t|| <= K because the difference quotients are bounded by K. deriv W is measurable (measurable_deriv). Hence ||deriv W|| and ||deriv W||^2 are integrable on (-a, a); ||W|| and ||W||^2 are integrable on (-a, a) since W is continuous on the compact interval [-a, a].
5. Fundamental theorem of calculus. For s, t in [-a, a]: ||W(t) - W(s)|| <= ∫_{(-a,a)} ||deriv W||. If W(t) = W(s) this is clear. Otherwise let u := (W(t) - W(s))/||W(t) - W(s)|| and φ(r) := <W(r), u>. Then φ is K-Lipschitz on [-a, a], hence absolutely continuous on uIcc s t (LipschitzOnWith.absolutelyContinuousOnInterval), so ∫_s^t deriv φ = φ(t) - φ(s) = ||W(t) - W(s)|| (AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval.integral_deriv_eq_sub). At every r in (-a, a) where W is differentiable, deriv φ r = <deriv W r, u>, so |deriv φ r| <= ||deriv W r|| for almost every r between s and t. Therefore ||W(t) - W(s)|| = ∫_s^t deriv φ <= ∫_{uIoc s t} |deriv φ| <= ∫_{uIoc s t} ||deriv W|| <= ∫_{(-a,a)} ||deriv W|| (the integrand is nonnegative, uIoc s t ⊆ [-a, a], and the endpoints are null).
6. Averaging. Fix x in B̄_a(0) and let t := x 0, so t in [-a, a] and ι t = x. By step 5, ||W(t)|| <= ||W(s)|| + D for every s in (-a, a), where D := ∫_{(-a,a)} ||deriv W||. Integrating over s in (-a, a), an interval of length 2a, and dividing by 2a: ||W(t)|| <= (2a)^{-1} ∫_{(-a,a)} ||W|| + D.
7. Cauchy-Schwarz on (-a, a): ∫ ||W|| <= (2a)^{1/2} (∫ ||W||^2)^{1/2} and D <= (2a)^{1/2} (∫ ||deriv W||^2)^{1/2}. Hence ||W(t)|| <= ((2a)^{-1} ∫_{(-a,a)} ||W||^2)^{1/2} + (2a ∫_{(-a,a)} ||deriv W||^2)^{1/2}.
8. Back to R^1. By steps 1 and 3, ∫_{(-a,a)} ||W(s)||^2 ds = ∫_{B_a(0)} ||w y||^2 dy and ∫_{(-a,a)} ||deriv W s||^2 ds = ∫_{B_a(0)} hsNormSq(fderiv w y) dy, and ||w(x)|| = ||W(t)||. This is the claim.
proof_key_steps: Transfer to W := w ∘ ι on [-a, a] by the measure-preserving isometry ι(t) = t e, with hsNormSq(fderiv w (ι t)) = ||deriv W t||^2
Rademacher: deriv W exists a.e. on (-a, a), is bounded by K and measurable
FTC for the absolutely continuous scalar function <W, u>: ||W(t) - W(s)|| <= ∫_{(-a,a)} ||deriv W||
Average over s and apply Cauchy-Schwarz, then transfer back to B_a(0)

subproblems.title: Scaling and Hoelder bounds for the scaled L^p norm of the mean curvature
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U any subset of R^{n+l}, V a contract rectifiable n-varifold in U with weight μ, H : R^{n+l} -> R^{n+l}, and K(y, r) := V.scaledLpNorm H p y r = (r^{p-n} ∫⁻_{B̄_r(y)} ||H||^p dμ)^{1/p} in [0, ∞] (closed balls; lower integrals; no measurability assumption on H). (a) If p > 0, 0 < s <= t and B̄_s(z) ⊆ B̄_t(w), then K(z, s) <= (s/t)^{(p-n)/p} K(w, t). (b) If 0 < q <= p, t > 0, m >= 0, B̄_s(z) ⊆ B̄_t(w) and μ(B̄_s(z)) <= m, then ∫⁻_{B̄_s(z)} ||H||^q dμ <= m^{1-q/p} t^{q(n-p)/p} K(w, t)^q.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (p : ℝ) (z w : Amb n ℓ) (s t : ℝ), 0 < p → 0 < s → s ≤ t → closedBall z s ⊆ closedBall w t → V.scaledLpNorm H p z s ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((s / t) ^ ((p - n) / p)) * V.scaledLpNorm H p w t) ∧ (∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (p q : ℝ) (z w : Amb n ℓ) (s t m : ℝ), 0 < q → q ≤ p → 0 < t → 0 ≤ m → closedBall z s ⊆ closedBall w t → V.weight (closedBall z s) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal m → ∫⁻ x in closedBall z s, ‖H x‖ₑ ^ q ∂V.weight ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (m ^ (1 - q / p) * t ^ (q * (n - p) / p)) * V.scaledLpNorm H p w t ^ q)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: μ := V.weight; I(y, r) := ∫⁻_{B̄_r(y)} ‖H‖ₑ^p dμ in [0, ∞], so K(y, r) = (ofReal(r^{p-n}) · I(y, r))^{1/p}. Real powers of positive reals are Real.rpow; powers of elements of [0, ∞] are ENNReal.rpow.
Part (a).
1. B̄_s(z) ⊆ B̄_t(w) gives I(z, s) <= I(w, t) (monotonicity of the lower integral in the domain, lintegral_mono_set).
2. As 0 < s <= t, s/t > 0 and s^{p-n} = (s/t)^{p-n} t^{p-n} (Real.div_rpow), so ofReal(s^{p-n}) = ofReal((s/t)^{p-n}) · ofReal(t^{p-n}) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, nonnegative factors).
3. Hence ofReal(s^{p-n}) I(z, s) <= ofReal((s/t)^{p-n}) · (ofReal(t^{p-n}) I(w, t)). The map x |-> x^{1/p} on [0, ∞] is monotone (1/p > 0, ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow) and multiplicative (ENNReal.mul_rpow_of_nonneg), so K(z, s) <= ofReal((s/t)^{p-n})^{1/p} · K(w, t).
4. ofReal((s/t)^{p-n})^{1/p} = ofReal(((s/t)^{p-n})^{1/p}) (ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_nonneg) = ofReal((s/t)^{(p-n)/p}) (Real.rpow_mul for the nonnegative base s/t; (p - n)(1/p) = (p - n)/p). This proves (a).
Part (b). Here p >= q > 0, so p > 0 and 0 <= 1 - q/p < 1.
5. Hoelder on B := B̄_s(z): for every function g : R^{n+l} -> [0, ∞], measurable or not, ∫⁻_B g^q dμ <= (∫⁻_B g^p dμ)^{q/p} μ(B)^{1-q/p}. Proof: by exists_measurable_le_lintegral_eq (for g^q and the measure μ.restrict B) there is a measurable G <= g^q with ∫⁻_B G dμ = ∫⁻_B g^q dμ. Put G1 := G^{1/q}: G1 is measurable, G1 <= (g^q)^{1/q} = g, and G1^q = G (ENNReal.rpow_mul with (1/q) q = 1). If q = p, then ∫⁻_B G <= ∫⁻_B g^p, which is the claim because μ(B)^0 = 1. If q < p, Hoelder's inequality ENNReal.lintegral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq on μ.restrict B with the conjugate exponents P := p/q and Q := p/(p - q), applied to G1^q and the constant 1, gives ∫⁻_B G1^q <= (∫⁻_B (G1^q)^P)^{1/P} (∫⁻_B 1)^{1/Q} = (∫⁻_B G1^p)^{q/p} μ(B)^{1-q/p} <= (∫⁻_B g^p)^{q/p} μ(B)^{1-q/p}, using G1 <= g and the monotonicity of the lower integral and of x |-> x^{q/p}.
6. Step 5 with g := ‖H‖ₑ, step 1, the hypothesis μ(B̄_s(z)) <= ofReal m and the monotonicity of x |-> x^{q/p} and x |-> x^{1-q/p} (nonnegative exponents) give ∫⁻_{B̄_s(z)} ‖H‖ₑ^q dμ <= I(z, s)^{q/p} μ(B̄_s(z))^{1-q/p} <= I(w, t)^{q/p} ofReal(m)^{1-q/p}.
7. ofReal(m)^{1-q/p} = ofReal(m^{1-q/p}) (m >= 0 and 1 - q/p >= 0; ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_nonneg).
8. Since t > 0, ofReal(t^{n-p}) · ofReal(t^{p-n}) = ofReal(t^{(n-p)+(p-n)}) = 1 (Real.rpow_add), so I(w, t) = ofReal(t^{n-p}) · (ofReal(t^{p-n}) I(w, t)), and by ENNReal.mul_rpow_of_nonneg, I(w, t)^{q/p} = ofReal(t^{n-p})^{q/p} · (ofReal(t^{p-n}) I(w, t))^{q/p}. Here ofReal(t^{n-p})^{q/p} = ofReal((t^{n-p})^{q/p}) = ofReal(t^{q(n-p)/p}) (Real.rpow_mul, t > 0), and (ofReal(t^{p-n}) I(w, t))^{q/p} = ((ofReal(t^{p-n}) I(w, t))^{1/p})^q = K(w, t)^q (ENNReal.rpow_mul, (1/p) q = q/p). These identities hold in [0, ∞] also when I(w, t) = ∞.
9. Combining steps 6 to 8 with ofReal(m^{1-q/p}) · ofReal(t^{q(n-p)/p}) = ofReal(m^{1-q/p} t^{q(n-p)/p}) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, m^{1-q/p} >= 0) gives (b).
proof_key_steps: (a): monotonicity of the p-integral in the ball and s^{p-n} = (s/t)^{p-n} t^{p-n}, then take 1/p-th powers
(b): Hoelder on B̄_s(z) for an arbitrary [0,∞]-valued function via a measurable minorant with the same integral
Bound μ(B̄_s(z)) by m and the p-integral over B̄_s(z) by the one over B̄_t(w)
Rewrite (∫_{B̄_t(w)} ||H||^p)^{q/p} = t^{q(n-p)/p} K(w, t)^q

subproblems.title: Monotonicity of the tilt-excess under inclusion of balls
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U a subset of R^{n+l}, and V a contract rectifiable n-varifold in U such that x |-> V.tangentProj x is V.weight-a.e. strongly measurable. If 0 < s <= t, B̄_s(z) ⊆ B̄_t(w) ⊆ U (closed balls) and S is any linear subspace of R^{n+l}, then E(z, s, S) <= (t/s)^n E(w, t, S), where E = V.tiltExcess.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight → ∀ (z w : Amb n ℓ) (s t : ℝ) (S : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), 0 < s → s ≤ t → closedBall z s ⊆ closedBall w t → closedBall w t ⊆ U → V.tiltExcess z s S ≤ (t / s) ^ n * V.tiltExcess w t S
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: μ := V.weight, M := V.carrier, θ := V.mult, N := n + l, and φ(x) := hsNormSq(V.tangentProj x - S.starProjection) >= 0.
1. Boundedness. For every x, ||V.tangentProj x|| <= 1: by definition V.tangentProj x is either P.starProjection for some subspace P (an orthogonal projection, operator norm <= 1) or 0. Also ||S.starProjection|| <= 1. For an operator B on R^N, hsNormSq B = sum_{i<N} ||B e_i||^2 <= N ||B||^2. Hence 0 <= φ(x) <= 4N for every x.
2. Measurability. B |-> hsNormSq B is continuous (a finite sum of squared norms of the continuous evaluations B |-> B e_i), and x |-> V.tangentProj x - S.starProjection is μ-a.e. strongly measurable by hypothesis; hence φ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
3. Finite measure. K := B̄_t(w) is compact and K ⊆ U. By the definition of the weight and withDensity_apply (K measurable), μ(K) = ∫⁻_{K ∩ M} ofReal(θ) dμHE[n] <= ∫⁻_{K ∩ M} ‖θ‖ₑ dμHE[n] < ∞, because θ is μHE[n]-integrable on M ∩ K (structure field integrableOn_mult).
4. Hence φ is μ-integrable on B̄_t(w) (bounded, a.e. strongly measurable, finite measure). As φ >= 0 and B̄_s(z) ⊆ B̄_t(w), ∫_{B̄_s(z)} φ dμ <= ∫_{B̄_t(w)} φ dμ (setIntegral_mono_set).
5. As 0 < s <= t, (s^n)^{-1} > 0 and (s^n)^{-1} = (t/s)^n (t^n)^{-1}. Therefore E(z, s, S) = (s^n)^{-1} ∫_{B̄_s(z)} φ dμ <= (s^n)^{-1} ∫_{B̄_t(w)} φ dμ = (t/s)^n ((t^n)^{-1} ∫_{B̄_t(w)} φ dμ) = (t/s)^n E(w, t, S).
proof_key_steps: The integrand hsNormSq(p_x - p_S) is bounded by 4(n+l) and a.e. strongly measurable
B̄_t(w) is a compact subset of U, so it has finite weight
Monotonicity of the set integral of a nonnegative integrable function

subproblems.title: Reduction to a plane of small tilt and small height (Simon 4.5, proof steps (1), (2))
subproblems.statement: Assume the contract Prop AffineApproximationLemma (Simon 2.5). For n >= 1, l and p > n there is C > 0, depending only on n, l, p, with the property: if U is open, V is a contract rectifiable n-varifold in U, H : R^{n+l} -> R^{n+l}, 0 < δ <= 1/4, AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ hold, x |-> V.tangentProj x is V.weight-a.e. strongly measurable, and μ(B̄_{δρ}(0)) >= ω_n (δρ)^n / 2 (μ = V.weight, ω_n = unitBallVolume n), then for every n-dimensional subspace T there is an n-dimensional subspace T' with E_*(0, δρ, T') <= E_*(0, δρ, T), E(0, δρ, T') <= C (δ^γ)^2, and dist(x, T') <= C δ^γ (δρ) for all x in spt V ∩ B̄_{2δρ}(0), where γ = 1/(2n+2), E = V.tiltExcess and E_* = V.tiltExcessStar H p δ.
subproblems.lean_statement: AffineApproximationLemma → ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (δ ρ : ℝ), 0 < δ → δ ≤ 1 / 4 → V.AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ → AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight → ENNReal.ofReal (unitBallVolume n * (δ * ρ) ^ n / 2) ≤ V.weight (closedBall 0 (δ * ρ)) → ∀ T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ T = n → ∃ T' : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ T' = n ∧ V.tiltExcessStar H p δ 0 (δ * ρ) T' ≤ V.tiltExcessStar H p δ 0 (δ * ρ) T ∧ V.tiltExcess 0 (δ * ρ) T' ≤ C * (δ ^ (1 / (2 * (n : ℝ) + 2))) ^ 2 ∧ ∀ x ∈ V.support ∩ closedBall 0 (2 * (δ * ρ)), infDist x (T' : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ C * δ ^ (1 / (2 * (n : ℝ) + 2)) * (δ * ρ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: γ := 1/(2n+2), so 0 < γ <= 1/4; σ := δρ; μ := V.weight; p_x := V.tangentProj x; for a subspace P, p_P := P.starProjection, E(P) := V.tiltExcess 0 σ P = σ^{-n} ∫_{B̄_σ(0)} hsNormSq(p_x - p_P) dμ and E_*(P) := V.tiltExcessStar H p δ 0 σ P = max{E(P), Y} with Y := δ^{-1} (V.scaledLpNorm H p 0 σ).toReal^2 (Y does not depend on P); ω := unitBallVolume n > 0; K(y, r) := V.scaledLpNorm H p y r.
Constants: let C_A > 0 be the constant given by AffineApproximationLemma for (n, l, p); put C_2 := 2^n C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2, C_3 := 2 C_A + 2 (8 C_2/ω)^{1/2} and C := max{C_2, C_3} > 0.
1. Preliminaries. By AllardHypotheses: ρ > 0, 0 ∈ spt V, B̄_ρ(0) ⊆ U, μ(B̄_ρ(0)) <= ofReal((1+δ) ω ρ^n) < ∞ and K(0, ρ) <= ofReal δ. As 0 < δ <= 1/4: σ > 0 and 2σ <= ρ/2 < ρ.
(1a) K(0, 2σ) <= ofReal δ: by tdo_scaledLpNorm_bounds part (a) with z = w = 0, s = 2σ, t = ρ (p > n >= 1 > 0), K(0, 2σ) <= ofReal((2σ/ρ)^{(p-n)/p}) K(0, ρ) <= ofReal δ, since 0 < 2σ/ρ <= 1 and (p - n)/p > 0 give (2σ/ρ)^{(p-n)/p} <= 1.
(1b) δ <= δ^γ, because 0 < δ <= 1 and 0 < γ <= 1.
2. Affine approximation. Apply AffineApproximationLemma (hypotheses: U open, 0 < δ <= 1/4, AllardHypotheses) at ξ := 0, which lies in spt V ∩ B̄_{δρ}(0), with radius σ_2 := 2δρ in (0, 2δρ]: there is a subspace T~ with finrank n such that
(2a) ofReal(C_A^{-1} sqrt((σ_2^n)^{-1} ∫_{B̄_{σ_2/2}(0)} hsNormSq(p_x - p_T~) dμ)) <= ofReal(σ_2^{-1}) · heightSup(0, σ_2, T~) + K(0, σ_2),
(2b) ofReal(σ_2^{-1}) · heightSup(0, σ_2, T~) <= ofReal(C_A δ^γ),
where σ_2 = 2σ and σ_2/2 = σ.
3. Height for T~. For x in spt V ∩ B̄_{2σ}(0), ofReal(infDist(x - 0, T~)) <= heightSup(0, 2σ, T~) (le_biSup), so (2b) gives ofReal((2σ)^{-1} infDist(x, T~)) <= ofReal(C_A δ^γ), i.e. infDist(x, T~) <= 2 C_A δ^γ σ.   (H~)
4. Tilt for T~. Let J~ := ∫_{B̄_σ(0)} hsNormSq(p_x - p_T~) dμ >= 0. By (2b), (1a), (1b), the right side of (2a) is <= ofReal(C_A δ^γ) + ofReal(δ^γ) = ofReal((C_A + 1) δ^γ). Hence C_A^{-1} sqrt((2σ)^{-n} J~) <= (C_A + 1) δ^γ (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff, the right side being >= 0), so (2σ)^{-n} J~ <= C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2 (δ^γ)^2 (square both nonnegative sides), and E(T~) = σ^{-n} J~ = 2^n (2σ)^{-n} J~ <= C_2 (δ^γ)^2.   (E~)
5. Case A: E(T) > C_2 (δ^γ)^2. Take T' := T~. Then finrank T' = n; E(T~) <= C_2 (δ^γ)^2 < E(T), hence E_*(T~) = max{E(T~), Y} <= max{E(T), Y} = E_*(T); E(T') <= C_2 (δ^γ)^2 <= C (δ^γ)^2; and by (H~), infDist(x, T') <= 2 C_A δ^γ σ <= C_3 δ^γ σ <= C δ^γ σ for x in spt V ∩ B̄_{2σ}(0).
6. Case B: E(T) <= C_2 (δ^γ)^2. Take T' := T. Then finrank T' = n, E_*(T') <= E_*(T) trivially, and E(T') <= C_2 (δ^γ)^2 <= C (δ^γ)^2. It remains to bound the height.
(6a) Integrability. For P in {T, T~}, φ_P(x) := hsNormSq(p_x - p_P) is μ-integrable on B̄_σ(0): it is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (hsNormSq is continuous and x |-> p_x is a.e. strongly measurable by hypothesis), it is bounded by 4(n+l) (||p_x|| <= 1 because by definition p_x is an orthogonal projection or 0, ||p_P|| <= 1, and hsNormSq B <= (n+l) ||B||^2), and μ(B̄_σ(0)) <= μ(B̄_ρ(0)) < ∞.
(6b) Let D := p_T - p_T~. For every x, D = (p_x - p_T~) - (p_x - p_T), so hsNormSq D <= 2 φ_T(x) + 2 φ_T~(x) (apply ||u - v||^2 <= 2||u||^2 + 2||v||^2 to each column D e_i).
(6c) Integrating (6b) over B̄_σ(0), using (6a): μ(B̄_σ(0)).toReal · hsNormSq D <= 2 σ^n E(T) + 2 σ^n E(T~) <= 4 C_2 (δ^γ)^2 σ^n, by Case B and (E~).
(6d) By hypothesis ofReal(ω σ^n/2) <= μ(B̄_σ(0)) < ∞, so μ(B̄_σ(0)).toReal >= ω σ^n/2 > 0. Hence hsNormSq D <= 8 C_2 (δ^γ)^2/ω and hsNorm D = sqrt(hsNormSq D) <= (8 C_2/ω)^{1/2} δ^γ.
(6e) For every y, ||D y|| <= hsNorm D ||y|| (write y = sum_i y_i e_i and use Cauchy-Schwarz).
(6f) Let x in spt V ∩ B̄_{2σ}(0). Since p_T x ∈ T, infDist(x, T) <= ||x - p_T x|| <= ||x - p_T~ x|| + ||D x||. The orthogonal projection onto the closed subspace T~ gives a nearest point, so ||x - p_T~ x|| = infDist(x, T~) <= 2 C_A δ^γ σ by (H~). With (6d), (6e) and ||x|| <= 2σ: infDist(x, T) <= 2 C_A δ^γ σ + (8 C_2/ω)^{1/2} δ^γ (2σ) = C_3 δ^γ σ <= C δ^γ σ.
7. In both cases T' has all the required properties, and C depends only on n, l, p.
proof_key_steps: K(0, 2δρ) <= δ by the scaling bound, and δ <= δ^γ
Affine approximation 2.5 at ξ = 0, radius 2δρ: plane T~ with height <= 2 C_A δ^γ δρ and E(0, δρ, T~) <= C_2 (δ^γ)^2
If E(0, δρ, T) > C_2 (δ^γ)^2 take T' = T~ (then E_* does not increase)
Otherwise take T' = T; the lower mass bound gives |p_T - p_T~| <= (8 C_2/ω_n)^{1/2} δ^γ and hence the height bound C_3 δ^γ δρ for T

subproblems.title: Height excess of a varifold near a rotated Lipschitz graph (Simon 4.5, proof step (20a))
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U ⊆ R^{n+l}, V a contract rectifiable n-varifold in U with weight μ, multiplicity θ and support spt V; q a linear isometry equivalence of R^{n+l}; f : R^n -> R^l; c in R^l; A : R^n -> R^l continuous linear; R, r, h, β real. Put τ := q(graphPoint(0, c)), S := span{q(graphPoint(v, A v)) : v in R^n}, λ(x') := c + A x' and Γ := q '' graphOver f B̄^n_R(0). Assume 0 < r <= R, B̄_R(0) ⊆ U, f is 1-Lipschitz on B̄^n_R(0), B̄_r(τ) ⊆ B̄_R(0), β >= 0, θ <= 2 μ-a.e. on B̄_r(τ), dist(x - τ, S) <= h for every x in spt V ∩ B̄_r(τ), and μ(B̄_R(0) ∩ (spt V \ Γ)) <= β. Then ∫_{B̄_r(τ)} dist(x - τ, S)^2 dμ <= 2 · 2^{n/2} ∫_{B^n_r(0)} ||f - λ||^2 dL^n + h^2 β, where B^n_r(0) is the open ball and dist = infDist.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (c : Rn ℓ) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (R r h β : ℝ), 0 < r → r ≤ R → closedBall 0 R ⊆ U → LipschitzOnWith 1 f (closedBall (0 : Rn n) R) → closedBall (q (graphPoint (0 : Rn n) c)) r ⊆ closedBall 0 R → 0 ≤ β → (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, x ∈ closedBall (q (graphPoint (0 : Rn n) c)) r → V.mult x ≤ 2) → (∀ x ∈ V.support ∩ closedBall (q (graphPoint (0 : Rn n) c)) r, infDist (x - q (graphPoint (0 : Rn n) c)) (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => q (graphPoint v (A v))) : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ h) → V.weight (closedBall 0 R ∩ (V.support \ q '' graphOver f (closedBall 0 R))) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal β → ∫ x in closedBall (q (graphPoint (0 : Rn n) c)) r, infDist (x - q (graphPoint (0 : Rn n) c)) (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => q (graphPoint v (A v))) : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ^ 2 ∂V.weight ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt 2 ^ n * (∫ x' in ball (0 : Rn n) r, ‖f x' - (c + A x')‖ ^ 2) + h ^ 2 * β
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: μ := V.weight, M := V.carrier, θ := V.mult, H^n := μHE[n] on R^{n+l}; τ, S, λ, Γ as in the statement; d(x) := infDist(x - τ, S); B := B̄_r(τ); F(x') := q(graphPoint x' (f x')), so Γ = F(B̄^n_R(0)).
1. Facts about μ.
(1a) μ-a.e. point lies in spt V. Indeed μ(μ.support^c) = 0 (measure_compl_support; R^{n+l} is second countable), and μ = (H^n.restrict M).withDensity(ofReal ∘ θ) is absolutely continuous with respect to H^n.restrict M, for which almost every point lies in the null-measurable set M ⊆ U (ae_restrict_mem₀); as spt V = U ∩ μ.support, μ-a.e. point lies in spt V. Consequently μ(E) <= μ(E ∩ spt V) for every set E (subadditivity and μ((spt V)^c) = 0).
(1b) μ(B̄_R(0)) < ∞: B̄_R(0) is compact and contained in U, and μ(B̄_R(0)) = ∫⁻_{M ∩ B̄_R(0)} ofReal(θ) dH^n <= ∫⁻_{M ∩ B̄_R(0)} ‖θ‖ₑ dH^n < ∞ by the structure field integrableOn_mult. Hence μ(B) < ∞.
(1c) For every measurable E ⊆ B and measurable g >= 0: ∫⁻_E g dμ <= 2 ∫⁻_E g dH^n. Indeed ∫⁻_E g dμ = ∫⁻_E g · ofReal(θ) d(H^n.restrict M) (lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul₀; θ is AEMeasurable for H^n.restrict M by the field aemeasurable_mult). The hypothesis that θ <= 2 μ-a.e. on B means, by ae_withDensity_iff', that for H^n.restrict M-a.e. x: ofReal(θ x) ≠ 0 implies (x ∈ B → θ x <= 2). Hence g · ofReal(θ) <= 2 g holds H^n.restrict M-a.e. on E (where ofReal(θ x) = 0 the left side vanishes), and integrating and using H^n.restrict M <= H^n gives the claim.
2. Measurability and bounds. d is 1-Lipschitz, hence continuous and Borel. F is continuous on the compact set B̄^n_R(0) (f is Lipschitz there; graphPoint and q are continuous), so Γ is compact, hence closed and measurable. For x in B, 0 <= d(x) <= ||x - τ|| <= r because 0 ∈ S.
3. The part on Γ. Let g := indicator of B times ofReal(d^2) (measurable). By (1c) with E := B ∩ Γ, ∫⁻_{B ∩ Γ} ofReal(d^2) dμ <= 2 ∫⁻_{B ∩ Γ} ofReal(d^2) dH^n = 2 ∫⁻_Γ g dH^n. By tdo_graph_lintegral_le (D := B̄^n_R(0), measurable; L := 1, f being 1-Lipschitz on D; sqrt(1 + 1^2) = sqrt 2), ∫⁻_Γ g dH^n <= ofReal(sqrt(2)^n) ∫⁻_{B̄^n_R(0)} g(F x') dx'. Let x' in B̄^n_R(0). If F x' ∉ B then g(F x') = 0. If F x' ∈ B then, by tdo_graph_plane_dist (iv) with y := f x', ||x'|| <= ||F x' - τ|| <= r, and by tdo_graph_plane_dist (iii), d(F x') <= ||f x' - λ(x')||. Hence g(F x') <= (indicator of B̄^n_r(0))(x') · ofReal(||f x' - λ(x')||^2) for every x' in B̄^n_R(0), and ∫⁻_{B̄^n_R(0)} g∘F <= ∫⁻_{B̄^n_r(0)} ofReal(||f - λ||^2). The sphere {||x'|| = r} is Lebesgue-null (r ≠ 0, Measure.addHaar_sphere_of_ne_zero), so the last integral equals ∫⁻_{B^n_r(0)} ofReal(||f - λ||^2). As r <= R, f - λ is continuous on B̄^n_r(0), so ||f - λ||^2 is bounded and integrable on the bounded set B^n_r(0), and ∫⁻_{B^n_r(0)} ofReal(||f - λ||^2) = ofReal(X) with X := ∫_{B^n_r(0)} ||f - λ||^2 >= 0 (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal). Altogether ∫⁻_{B ∩ Γ} ofReal(d^2) dμ <= ofReal(2 sqrt(2)^n X).
4. The part off Γ. By (1a), μ-a.e. x in B \ Γ lies in spt V ∩ B, where 0 <= d(x) <= h by hypothesis; so ofReal(d(x)^2) <= ofReal(h^2) for μ-a.e. x in B \ Γ, and ∫⁻_{B \ Γ} ofReal(d^2) dμ <= ofReal(h^2) μ(B \ Γ). By (1a), μ(B \ Γ) <= μ((B \ Γ) ∩ spt V) <= μ(B̄_R(0) ∩ (spt V \ Γ)) <= ofReal β, since B ⊆ B̄_R(0). Hence ∫⁻_{B \ Γ} ofReal(d^2) dμ <= ofReal(h^2) ofReal(β) = ofReal(h^2 β) (β >= 0).
5. As Γ is measurable, ∫⁻_B ofReal(d^2) dμ = ∫⁻_{B ∩ Γ} ofReal(d^2) dμ + ∫⁻_{B \ Γ} ofReal(d^2) dμ <= ofReal(2 sqrt(2)^n X) + ofReal(h^2 β) = ofReal(2 sqrt(2)^n X + h^2 β), both arguments being >= 0.
6. d^2 is continuous and bounded by r^2 on B and μ(B) < ∞ (1b), so d^2 is μ-integrable on B and ∫_B d^2 dμ = (∫⁻_B ofReal(d^2) dμ).toReal <= 2 sqrt(2)^n X + h^2 β (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae, ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal). Since sqrt(2)^n = 2^{n/2}, this is the claim.
proof_key_steps: μ-a.e. point lies in spt V; B̄_R(0) has finite weight; θ <= 2 on B̄_r(τ) gives μ <= 2 H^n there
On Γ: the area bound tdo_graph_lintegral_le with L = 1 and the graph-plane estimates (iii), (iv) bound the integral by 2 · 2^{n/2} ∫_{B^n_r(0)} ||f - λ||^2
Off Γ: μ-a.e. such point is in spt V \ Γ, where dist <= h, and that set has weight <= β
Add the two parts and convert the lower integral back to the Bochner integral

subproblems.title: Sup height of the support from a graph sup bound and a lower density bound
subproblems.statement: Let n, l, U, V (weight μ, support spt V), q, f, c, A be as in tdo_graph_height_excess, with τ := q(graphPoint(0, c)), S := span{q(graphPoint(v, A v)) : v in R^n}, λ(x') := c + A x' and Γ := q '' graphOver f B̄^n_R(0), and let R, a, r, s₀, b, β, κ be real numbers with b >= 0, κ > 0, r + s₀ <= a and ||c|| + r + s₀ <= R. Assume: ||f(x') - λ(x')|| <= b for all x' in B̄^n_a(0); μ(B̄_R(0) ∩ (spt V \ Γ)) <= β; μ(B̄_s(x)) >= κ s for all x in spt V ∩ B̄_r(τ) and 0 < s <= s₀; and dist(x - τ, S) <= 2 s₀ for all x in spt V ∩ B̄_r(τ). Then dist(x - τ, S) <= max{2b, 2β/κ} for every x in spt V ∩ B̄_r(τ) (dist = infDist, closed balls).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: μ := V.weight; τ, S, λ, Γ as in the statement; d(x) := infDist(x - τ, S); F(x') := q(graphPoint x' (f x')), so Γ = F(B̄^n_R(0)).
1. μ-a.e. point lies in spt V: μ(μ.support^c) = 0 (measure_compl_support), μ-a.e. point lies in the carrier M ⊆ U (μ is absolutely continuous with respect to μHE[n].restrict M and M is null-measurable; ae_restrict_mem₀), and spt V = U ∩ μ.support. Hence μ((spt V)^c) = 0 and μ(E) <= μ(E ∩ spt V) for every set E.
2. Fix x in spt V ∩ B̄_r(τ) and put h_x := d(x) >= 0. By hypothesis h_x <= 2 s₀, so s₀ >= 0 and r <= r + s₀ <= a. By tdo_graph_plane_dist (v), ||τ|| = ||c||, so ||x|| <= ||c|| + r. If h_x <= 2b, then h_x <= max{2b, 2β/κ} and we are done; assume from now on h_x > 2b.
3. x ∉ Γ. Otherwise x = F(x') with x' in B̄^n_R(0); by tdo_graph_plane_dist (iv) with y := f x', ||x'|| <= ||x - τ|| <= r <= a, so x' ∈ B̄^n_a(0), and by tdo_graph_plane_dist (iii), h_x <= ||f x' - λ(x')|| <= b <= 2b (b >= 0), contradicting h_x > 2b.
4. Let s := h_x/2. Then s > b >= 0 and s <= s₀. Claim: B̄_s(x) ∩ Γ = ∅. Suppose y ∈ B̄_s(x) ∩ Γ, y = F(y') with y' in B̄^n_R(0). By tdo_graph_plane_dist (iv), ||y'|| <= ||y - τ|| <= ||y - x|| + ||x - τ|| <= s + r <= s₀ + r <= a, so y' ∈ B̄^n_a(0), and by tdo_graph_plane_dist (iii), d(y) <= ||f y' - λ(y')|| <= b < s. Since infDist(·, S) is 1-Lipschitz, h_x = d(x) <= d(y) + ||(x - τ) - (y - τ)|| = d(y) + ||x - y|| < s + s = h_x, a contradiction.
5. B̄_s(x) ⊆ B̄_R(0): for z in B̄_s(x), ||z|| <= ||x|| + s <= ||c|| + r + s₀ <= R.
6. By the lower density hypothesis (x ∈ spt V ∩ B̄_r(τ), 0 < s <= s₀), ofReal(κ s) <= μ(B̄_s(x)). By steps 1, 4 and 5, μ(B̄_s(x)) <= μ(B̄_s(x) ∩ spt V) <= μ(B̄_R(0) ∩ (spt V \ Γ)) <= ofReal β. So ofReal(κ s) <= ofReal β with κ s > 0; hence ofReal β > 0, so β > 0 and κ s <= β (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff). Therefore h_x = 2s <= 2β/κ <= max{2b, 2β/κ}.
proof_key_steps: μ-a.e. point lies in spt V
A support point on Γ near τ has height <= b by the graph-plane estimates (iii), (iv)
If the height h_x of a support point exceeds 2b, the ball B̄_{h_x/2}(x) misses Γ and lies in B̄_R(0)
Lower density on that ball and the bound on the weight of spt V \ Γ give κ h_x/2 <= β
